subject: Which events count? midday log timestamps & audit-day inclusivity
messages:
From: Eleni Papadopoulos <eleni@brightbridge-audit.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification needed — day boundary and timestamp format for point-in-time evidence

Hi Hannah,

We're preparing the procedures for the Type II fieldwork and need to confirm a few specifics about how Redwood interprets an "audit day" and how that maps to the log evidence you'll provide. The SOC 2 report we have references the audit period ending 2025-06-30, but some of the system logs are recorded in local server time and some are stored as UTC. To avoid sampling errors, can you confirm the following: 

- Do you consider the audit day (e.g., 2025-06-30) to include events timestamped up to 23:59:59 in local server time, or do you define inclusivity in UTC?
- For systems that report local time (PDT/PST), how do you reconcile those entries when we request a contiguous point-in-time window centered around midnight (e.g., 2025-06-30 23:50 to 2025-07-01 00:10)?
- Do daily backup snapshots and database dumps use a specific timestamp (e.g., completed at 02:00 UTC) that we should treat as the "snapshot" moment for point-in-time evidence?

For testing purposes, please provide a small, redacted log extract showing 10 minutes before and 10 minutes after 2025-06-30 23:59 in the format you would deliver evidence (include header row). Also attach the SOC 2 final report you referenced in the control mapping (if you can).

I've attached our preliminary workpaper checklist (evidence-checklist.xlsx) to help guide the extract format. If you prefer, we can accept logs normalized to UTC, but we need an explicit statement in your evidence package that indicates whether timestamps were converted and how (e.g., server-local -> UTC conversion using TZ database v2025a).

Thanks,
Eleni
Senior Manager, IT Audit
BrightBridge Audit
(attachment: SOC2-TYPEII-2024-report.pdf - stub)
(attachment: evidence-checklist.xlsx - stub)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eleni Papadopoulos <eleni@brightbridge-audit.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification needed — day boundary and timestamp format for point-in-time evidence

Hi Eleni — thanks for the sharp questions. Summary answers up front: we deliver evidence in UTC by default, our daily snapshots are taken at 02:00 UTC, and we will provide a short attestation explaining the conversion method. Details below and next steps.

Quick answers: 
- Audit-day inclusivity: Redwood treats the audit day as inclusive up to 23:59:59 UTC for evidence packages. We standardize to UTC before exporting any log slices for auditors.
- Local vs UTC reconciliation: we convert all server-local timestamps to UTC at export time, using system timezone metadata (we store the original local timestamp in a separate field). We'll include both the original local_time and normalized_utc_time columns in the extract.
- Snapshot timing: daily backups / point-in-time database snapshots complete at *~02:00 UTC*; we use the snapshot completion timestamp as the canonical time for rollforward/rollback evidence.

Attachments we will provide: a redacted log snippet for 2025-06-30 23:50:00 UTC -> 2025-07-01 00:10:00 UTC with header columns (original_local_time, normalized_utc_time, service, event_type, request_id, user_id_masked, message), the SOC2 final report you referenced (attached), and a draft bridge letter.

Can you confirm whether you want the extract in CSV or newline-delimited JSON? We can deliver both, but CSV is quicker. Also, please confirm whether your sampling will center on UTC midnight or on local midnight for servers that are not in the UTC timezone — we will include conversion artifacts either way, but the sampling approach affects how we slice correlated services across regions.

Proposed timeline: 
- End of day tomorrow (2025-07-30 17:00 PDT) we can send the redacted CSV extract and the bridge-letter-draft.docx for your review.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
(attachment: SOC2-TYPEII-2024-report.pdf - stub)

From: Eleni Papadopoulos <eleni@brightbridge-audit.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>, nimbus-compliance@nimbushealth.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification needed — day boundary and timestamp format for point-in-time evidence

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear summary, that helps a lot. CSV is fine. A couple of follow-ups: 

1) Please include both original_local_time and normalized_utc_time in the header, and add a short JSON "export_meta" line at the top of the CSV that indicates the timezone conversion method and the OS-level TZ database version (e.g., TZDB v2025a) — that will speed our automated parsing.

2) For sampling: we'll center the sample around *UTC midnight* for consistency across services. We'll request correlated slices for services with different host timezones, so including original_local_time is critical.

3) The bridge letter: please make it explicit that the exported logs were normalized to UTC for the purposes of sampling and that original_local_time values are preserved in a separate column. A short paragraph about snapshot completion at 02:00 UTC would be useful.

We can accept the draft bridge-letter-draft.docx; once we review we may send a couple of minor edits. Expect a short list of clarifying redlines from us after we receive the CSV.

Thanks — Eleni
(attachment: evidence-checklist.xlsx - stub)

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eleni Papadopoulos <eleni@brightbridge-audit.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification needed — day boundary and timestamp format for point-in-time evidence

Eleni / Hannah / Marcus — confirming next steps from Redwood: 

- We'll produce the redacted CSV extract (2025-06-30 23:50:00 -> 2025-07-01 00:10:00 UTC) with header row: export_meta,original_local_time,normalized_utc_time,service,event_type,request_id,user_id_masked,message. The export_meta will be a single JSON string describing conversion method and TZDB version.
- Attached: bridge-letter-draft.docx (please review and suggest edits), and a tiny log sample (log-sample-20250729-2358-0001.csv - stub) to show the exact format.
- Delivery: we'll upload the CSV and the final bridge letter draft to the Drive folder at https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-evidence by EOD 2025-07-30 (17:00 PDT). We'll also post a DocuSign link for a short attestation if you require signed confirmation of the normalization approach.

If that timeline works for BrightBridge and Nimbus, we'll proceed and mark the action item in our tracker. Marcus, please confirm logs run OK with the export job this afternoon and attach the sample when ready.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
(attachment: bridge-letter-draft.docx - stub)
(attachment: log-sample-20250729-2358-0001.csv - stub)
